data.long_meaning: Anowar is derived from the Sanskrit word 'anugha' meaning grace or help from God. It is a name bestowed upon those who seek divine protection and guidance. The name Anowar carries the meaning “God's Grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anowar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Anowar was a Bengali Muslim warrior who fought against the British East India Company during the Indian Rebellion of 1857. He was a leading figure in the rebellion in the districts of Nadia and 24 Parganas.

historical_references.reference: Anowar Shah II was a Sultan of Bengal in the late 13th century. He succeeded his father, Shamsuddin Iltutmish, and reigned for a brief period before being assassinated by his own courtiers.
